content:
Apple's new-generation M6 chip debuted last week alongside the new Mac mini. But several more products will be upgraded to M6 in the near future. Here's the rumored release timeline for the M6 Mac—and M6 iPad Pro.

This fall: M6 MacBook Pro, M6 iMac

Apple is reportedly set to launch two new M6 Macs this fall (likely in October or early November):

  • MacBook Pro
  • iMac

The MacBook Pro will only be the 14-inch base model. According to Mark Gurman, Apple will skip the M6 Pro and Max versions. Therefore, only the entry-level MacBook Pro will use M6, and the next batch of pro-level chips will be the M7 Pro and M7 Max arriving in 2027.

Apple's new iMac isn't expected to see major changes beyond the chip. The only other rumored upgrade is a range of new colors. But the jump from M4 to M6 should be enough to make the new machine worth upgrading.

Notably absent from this list is the rumored touch-screen MacBook Pro / Ultra. It is also expected to launch in the near future, but will use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than M6.

Early 2027: M6 MacBook Air, M6 iPad Pro

Following this fall, the next batch of products rumored to be upgraded to M6 includes:

  • MacBook Air
  • iPad Pro

The new M6 MacBook Air is expected to launch in early 2027. It could come anytime between February and April, but based on Apple's past practices, March is the safer bet.

Beyond the chip upgrade, there aren't many rumors about the new MacBook Air. It should carry over the same design as the M5 model. There are also reports that the OLED upgrade won't arrive until at least 2028, so the display will most likely remain unchanged.

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in fall 2025, when it was equipped with the M5 chip. Rumors point to an update in spring 2027, meaning the product will return to its usual 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond the M6 chip, Apple's new iPad Pro is expected to feature a vapor chamber cooling design. This update should boost sustained performance on this ultra-thin device.

For both the MacBook Air and iPad Pro, one potential benefit of M6 is improved battery life. Apple says the 2-nanometer process used in M6 brings "major leaps in performance and energy efficiency."

Are you planning to upgrade to any of these new M6 products? Why? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
